english.title: Landlord / agent harass occupier to give up premises
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the

(A)_[landlord]_
(B)_[agent of the landlord]_

of **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), the residential occupier of premises, namely **(..SPECIFY PREMISES..), did acts likely to interfere with the peace or comfort of the residential occupier or members of

(C)_[his]_
(D)_[her]_

household, namely **(..SPECIFY ACTS..), knowing or having reasonable cause to believe that such conduct was likely to cause the residential occupier to give up the occupation of the whole or part of the premises or to refrain from exercising any right or pursuing any remedy in respect of the whole or part of the premises
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(3A) and (4) of the Protection from Eviction Act 1977.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: A person may not be convicted of this offence, in respect of any conduct, where a civil financial penalty has been imposed by a local authority as an alternative to prosecution under section 1A.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6 / 12 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

(i) On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
(ii) The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 282(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.
